pillar_reactions.evidence: Rep described the mechanism inside the cheap tier — 'first one to two months are going to come down to really building the foundation... only then we're actually going to increase weight... but first going to go into your mobility, and that's going to help with overall longevity'. She did not question it and did not react to it; she came back only on price and on the missing one-to-one.

Pushed back on nutrition as a value driver: 'I'm getting that anyway, like with the nutrition and with that, all that stuff that you're saying' and later 'I'm aware of nutrition. I'm very careful with what I eat and all that... there's an abundance of information on Instagram about that.'

Rejected community-based accountability as a substitute for a coach: 'it's the push of the one-on-one knowing that my coach is like, you know, watching me as to my progression... that's the only way that I know that I'm going to improve'. She had already framed her whole problem this way — 'because I don't have a trainer I'm not motivated'.

anchors.raw: I was thinking like $1,000 a year, maybe I can, you know, can do something with that
anchors.note: Her self-declared ceiling is roughly a sixth of the six-month offer, and stated as an annual figure. The rep then priced a six-month tier at exactly $1,000, anchoring the programme to her number rather than the other way round.

anchors.raw: the Instagram has been saturated with coaches and what have you... some of them are ridiculous, some of them say you can pay as you go
anchors.note: Her reference class for online coaching is the Instagram coach market with pay-as-you-go billing, which sets both a low price expectation and an expectation of flexible payment before $6,000 is ever heard.

anchors.raw: I've just joined the gym which is just around the corner... I've paid and I haven't been
anchors.note: A recent gym membership she is not using is live evidence to her that paying for fitness does not convert into showing up — an anchor against spending more, which the rep never turned around.

anchors.raw: America is different as in the prices to the here
anchors.note: She expects US pricing not to apply in Australia. The rep answered with 'I just searched it up, Australia is 40% more', which argues the price should be higher rather than addressing her value concern.

unmet_demand.want: One-to-one coaching with a named human watching her form and progression, at a price near $1,000-$1,500
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only thing available at that price point is the self-guided community programme, and the one-to-one element is precisely what she says is the reason she cannot train alone.

unmet_demand.want: A lower-cost one-to-one tier delivered by someone other than Trevor
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep said this is being built — 'we are actually currently working on creating a coaching program that's still one-on-one, but actually with Trevor's second guy, that's Caden' — but it does not exist, has no price and no date.

unmet_demand.want: Pay-as-you-go or instalment billing rather than an upfront four-figure sum
unmet_demand.why_unmet: She asked directly, 'does he do have payment plans or anything like that', and got only 'yeah, like if needed we can always look into that'. No plan was ever structured or priced for her.
